evals.prompt: Our CTO wants a clear comparison matrix across **AWS CDK**, **Terraform / OpenTofu**, **AWS CloudFormation**, **Pulumi**, and **Crossplane** to standardize our AWS IaC strategy across two teams: (Team A) 15 TypeScript full-stack product engineers building serverless/container apps exclusively on AWS, and (Team B) a 5-person Kubernetes platform team running EKS + multi-cloud DNS/GitHub/Datadog providers. Recommend the best engine(s) with explicit trade-offs.
expectations: Activates the iac-architecture-advisor skill
Compares all 5 engines across language/abstraction model, state backend, drift/reconciliation model, policy-as-code ecosystem, and multi-cloud scope

Recommends **AWS CDK v2** (TypeScript L2 constructs + CloudFormation state) for Team A and **Terraform/OpenTofu** (for multi-provider AWS + DNS/GitHub/Datadog foundations) and/or **Crossplane** (if exposing Kubernetes-native self-service CRDs/Claims on EKS) for Team B

evals.prompt: A 2-person startup wants to prototype a greenfield Next.js SaaS MVP on AWS this week with reusable UI components + editable CDK backend constructs in their repo rather than writing low-level CloudFormation or locked-in wrappers. Which rapid-prototyping path should they pick (`aws-blocks` vs `launch-with-aws` vs raw Terraform), and why?
expectations: Activates the iac-architecture-advisor skill
Recommends **AWS Blocks** (`@aws-blocks/create-blocks-app` / `aws-blocks`) for greenfield full-stack Next.js/React rapid prototyping

Clearly distinguishes why `launch-with-aws` is NOT the primary fit here (`launch-with-aws` migrates existing non-AWS/PaaS apps like Heroku/Render/Vercel/Docker repos onto AWS) and why raw Terraform slows down full-stack UI+backend MVP velocity

evals.prompt: We have an existing production Express.js + PostgreSQL + Redis repository currently hosted on Render/Heroku (`render.yaml` / `Procfile`) and want an automated code + IaC migration plan onto AWS. Should we use `aws-blocks`, `launch-with-aws`, `aws-brownfield-migration`, or `Crossplane`?
expectations: Activates the iac-architecture-advisor skill

Evaluates `launch-with-aws` (for automated app/PaaS migration onto AWS) alongside production IaC engines (`aws-cdk` / `aws-terraform`) and explains why `aws-blocks`, `aws-brownfield-migration` (for unmanaged resources already in AWS), and `Crossplane` serve different roles

evals.prompt: A regulated financial institution mandates: (1) zero external SaaS state backends and zero S3 state files managed outside AWS control planes, (2) declarative YAML/JSON auditable templates with StackSets across 80 AWS Organizations accounts, and (3) no Node.js/Python runtime in air-gapped deploy runners. Recommend the right IaC engine and governance stack.
expectations: Activates the iac-architecture-advisor skill

Recommends native **AWS CloudFormation** (with **CloudFormation StackSets** for multi-account AWS Organizations rollout, **CloudFormation Guard (`cfn-guard`)** + CloudFormation Hooks, and AWS-managed stack state)
Explains why CDK/Pulumi require Node.js/Python runtimes (violating constraint 3) and why Terraform/OpenTofu requires self-managing S3 `.tfstate` buckets or external SaaS state

evals.prompt: Our platform engineering group runs ArgoCD on Amazon EKS and wants product teams to provision RDS databases, S3 buckets, and SQS queues simply by committing Kubernetes YAML manifests alongside their `Deployment` manifests — with continuous drift reconciliation. Evaluate Crossplane vs Terraform vs ACK (AWS Controllers for Kubernetes).
expectations: Activates the iac-architecture-advisor skill

Recommends **Crossplane** (with Upbound `provider-family-aws`, XRDs, and Pipeline Compositions) for multi-resource platform abstractions (`XDatabase` bundling RDS + SubnetGroup + SecurityGroup + Secrets) reconciled continuously via ArgoCD

Contrasts Crossplane against Terraform (CLI/CI run-based, no continuous control loop by default unless paired with paid drift runners) and ACK (1:1 low-level AWS API CRDs without built-in XRD composition pipelines)

evals.prompt: Our engineering org writes 100% TypeScript and loves real programming constructs, loops, and Vitest unit tests — and our stack spans AWS (ECS, Aurora, S3) PLUS Cloudflare DNS/WAF, Auth0, and GCP BigQuery in one unified IaC workflow. Compare AWS CDK vs CDKTF vs Pulumi TypeScript.
expectations: Activates the iac-architecture-advisor skill
Recommends **Pulumi (TypeScript)** (`@pulumi/aws` + `@pulumi/aws-native` + `@pulumi/cloudflare` + `@pulumi/gcp` + CrossGuard + Pulumi ESC) as the first-class multi-cloud TypeScript IaC engine

Explains why AWS CDK is AWS/CloudFormation-centric (requiring custom resources/extensions for non-AWS providers) and notes CDKTF ecosystem/maintenance trade-offs compared to native Pulumi or Terraform HCL

evals.prompt: Half our company (Cloud Ops) manages landing zones, Transit Gateways, VPCs, and IAM in Terraform, while 8 serverless product squads want to use AWS CDK or AWS SAM for their Lambda + Step Functions + DynamoDB microservices. Should we force everyone onto one tool, or run a layered hybrid model? Show how the boundary contract works cleanly.
expectations: Activates the iac-architecture-advisor skill

Endorses a clean **layered two-tier boundary** (Platform/Network/Landing-Zone foundation in Terraform; Product microservice stacks in AWS CDK / SAM) when each resource has a **single owning IaC engine**

Defines the loose-coupling contract via SSM Parameter Store (`/platform/vpc/private-subnet-ids`, `/platform/kms/arn`) or tag-based `data`/lookup queries — never dual-managing the same AWS resource across two engines

evals.prompt: Inspect `ap-south-1` in our live AWS account (read-only) to detect what IaC footprint already exists (e.g., CloudFormation stacks, `CDKToolkit`, `aws:cloudformation:stack-name` or `ManagedBy=Terraform`/`Pulumi` resource tags, S3 state buckets) and advise which IaC engine aligns best with the account's current state.
expectations: Activates the iac-architecture-advisor skill and performs read-only discovery in `ap-south-1` (`cloudformation list-stacks`/`describe-stacks`, tag/bucket inspection) via connected AWS MCP tools with zero raw `aws` CLI shell commands
Accurately summarizes the live `ap-south-1` IaC footprint and gives a grounded engine recommendation rather than guessing
Makes zero mutating AWS calls
